assertions.subject: Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
assertions.quote: For catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, nadolol is effective.

assertions.subject: Long QT syndrome
assertions.quote: Nadolol and propranolol are indicated for LQTS.

assertions.subject: Long QT syndrome
assertions.quote: Nadolol and propranolol are indicated for LQTS.

assertions.subject: Long QT syndrome type-3
assertions.quote: Mexiletine is used for LQTS type-3.

assertions.subject: Torsades de pointes in LQTS and Brugada syndrome
assertions.quote: Isoprenaline (isoproterenol) is helpful for torsades de pointes in LQTS and Brugada syndrome.

assertions.subject: Brugada syndrome
assertions.quote: Quinidine is prescribed for Brugada syndrome and SQTS.

assertions.subject: Short QT syndrome
assertions.quote: Quinidine is prescribed for Brugada syndrome and SQTS.

assertions.subject: Atrial fibrillation in older patients
assertions.quote: Using dronedarone is associated with poor outcomes in older patients, particularly those with permanent atrial fibrillation and decompensated heart failure.

assertions.subject: Atrial fibrillation in older patients
assertions.quote: Digoxin is not recommended as a first-line treatment for rate control in older patients with atrial fibrillation, as safer and more effective medications are available.

assertions.subject: Atrial fibrillation in older patients
assertions.quote: Amiodarone is an excellent antiarrhythmic agent but carries a higher toxicity risk than other antiarrhythmic drugs used in atrial fibrillation.
